workLog.task: Measure the acceptance criteria against the tree
workLog.outcome: Two of three already ship. check_skill_resolver_anchoring.py enforces absolute-top-level anchoring for SKILL.md resolvers and names the same installed-plugins stale-copy failure. check_skill_contract_tests.py enforces the test requirement for skill prose defining executable contracts. Neither had a rule stating the requirement.

workLog.task: Measure the worktree-identity hazard before writing the rule
workLog.outcome: core.worktree and GIT_WORK_TREE both redirect git rev-parse --show-toplevel, and git status then reports every tracked file as deleted. The three cases that would make it latent came back negative: git worktree add sets neither, a moved worktree still resolves, and a worktree whose main checkout moved away fails closed with a non-zero exit.

workLog.task: Decide against a runtime containment guard in get_repo_root
workLog.outcome: The redirection is always deliberate, nothing in this repository sets it, and the guard would have broken five tests in tests/test_repo_root.py plus a legitimate GIT_WORK_TREE invocation where cwd is outside the tree by design. Recorded the reasoning in .serena/memories/decision-worktree-identity-guard-scope.md.

workLog.task: Ship the rules and regenerate the mirrors
workLog.outcome: ci-scripts.md MUST 7 and MUST 8, claude-agents.md MUST 7, both instruction mirrors regenerated with build/scripts/generate_rules.py, both plugin manifests bumped to 0.6.128 (rebumped after main advanced to 0.6.127) and parity confirmed.

Corrupting .github/instructions/ci-scripts.instructions.md leaves tests/build_scripts/test_generate_rules.py green at 43 passed. build_all.py --check catches it with exit 2 and STALENESS DETECTED, and that is what lefthook and two workflows run. The generator's own tests are not the drift gate.
